title: Research on Multimodal Safety Risk Situation Awareness and Prevention Strategy for Major Projects Integrating Space‑Air‑Ground Remote Sensing Observations
content: Safety risks of large-scale water conservancy, transportation, and energy infrastructure emerge from coupled geological conditions, extreme weather events, and construction disturbances throughout construction and operation phases. These risks are characterized by concealment, wide-area distribution, and dynamic evolution. Limited by sensor deployment locations and personnel accessibility, conventional ground sensors and manual inspections struggle to detect regional geological hazards outside project boundaries. Space–air–ground remote sensing observations, including Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites, optical satellites, and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery, support wide-area non-contact monitoring and capture spatial information such as slope deformation, land cover anomalies, and landslide precursors. However, single-source remote sensing is vulnerable to cloud and fog contamination and temporal decorrelation. It also cannot reflect internal structural conditions, which demands feature-level fusion with ground-based monitoring data. This study takes multi-source remote sensing as the core modality and integrates ground-based time-series sensors, on-site audio-visual recordings, and engineering archive texts. A space–air–ground collaborative multimodal safety risk situational awareness framework is established for major infrastructure projects. Following the pipeline of feature extraction, cross-modal spatiotemporal alignment, and adaptive attention fusion, the framework enables risk perception, deduction and assessment, and forms a closed-loop prevention chain of “cognition–deduction–decision–optimization”. Simulations and field measurements show that the proposed model achieves an overall risk perception rate of 96%, early warning accuracy above 94%, and a 63% reduction in response latency compared with conventional schemes. The remote sensing branch achieves a recall rate of 92.7% for geological hazard identification. Ablation experiments demonstrate that removing remote sensing inputs reduces the overall perception rate to 90.2%, accompanied by a notable increase in undetected geological hazards. This work delivers a technical solution for intelligent risk prevention and control across the full life cycle of major projects. It advances the shift of engineering safety management from passive response to proactive early warning, and provides theoretical and practical support for remote sensing-enabled infrastructure safety monitoring.
